email.subject: Your parcel is ready to collect

body.v: Your parcel is ready to collect at the pick-up point. Collecting it costs nothing.
Bring the code shown in the ParcelPoint app.

hotspots.explain: The address is on parcelpoint.example, the real domain.
"Costs nothing" is the opposite of a fee scam.
It sends you to the app you already have.
A plain "Hello" is a little impersonal, but the domain is what counts here.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ParcelPoint: the address is on the real domain, parcelpoint.example.
choices: A scammer with a lookalike address

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. It is a calm notice with no deadline.
choices: None: it is a calm notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Collect your parcel. It costs nothing and there is no link or login.
choices: Collect the parcel, at no cost
Pay a fee through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself to see the pick-up point and your code.
choices: Reply and ask for the code

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and look at the pick-up details
actions.consequence: Your code and pick-up point are listed.

actions.label: Collect the parcel with the code from your app
actions.consequence: No money is asked for. It matches the app.

actions.label: Reply to ask for the code
actions.consequence: The no-reply address does not answer. The code is in your app.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear. Compare it with the 'fee due' message: the real one costs nothing, has no link and points you to the app. When money is not asked for, there is much less to worry about.
